column1: # What still differs between macOS and GNUstep in the corpus comparison
# (.tools/xp/compare.py, the xp job in build.yml), and why: one line per
# report and check -- id<TAB>check<TAB>reason; an id may be a glob.
# Checks: status, pages, text, pixels, html (compare.py says what each is).
# A difference listed here is reported and passed; one that is not fails the
# job. When a fix lands -- a gnustep-patches release moved in .github/pins.env
# -- the comparison says which lines no longer differ ("FIXED?" in
# verdict.txt), and they come out of this file.

a page of fractional height (8.3in = 597.6pt) is drawn by whole points on GNUstep: the page rect is cut to 842 x 597 and everything on it sits 0.6pt higher than on the Mac (waiting on gnustep-patches)
a page of fractional height (841.68pt) is drawn by whole points on GNUstep: the page rect is cut to 595 x 841 and everything on it sits 0.68pt higher than on the Mac (waiting on gnustep-patches)
not a fault on either side: the report asks for 8.27in x 11.69in = 595.44 x 841.68pt, which GNUstep writes; macOS snaps the sheet to its A4 (595 x 842) and centres the page on it
the turned "Matrix" label runs off the page, which shows only its "M": Quartz keeps the hidden rest of a line it draws in the PDF's text, cairo leaves out every glyph the clip hides

glyph rasterization: the text is in the same places at 300 dpi, but its pages are 2in tall and nothing but 10pt text, where poppler's anti-aliasing of the two PDFs' embedded fonts differs in 0.9% of the pixels at 60 dpi
